summary: Framework for scaling Python and AI workloads from a laptop to a cluster, with libraries for data, training, tuning and serving.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Ray is a unified framework for scaling AI and Python applications. It has a core distributed runtime plus AI libraries for data processing, distributed training, hyperparameter tuning, reinforcement learning and model serving.
sixtySeconds.problem: Modern ML workloads outgrow a single laptop. Ray lets you scale the same Python code from a laptop to a cluster without building other infrastructure.
whoFor: ML engineers training and serving models at scale
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for one general-purpose framework that runs on any machine, cluster, cloud provider or Kubernetes, with a big ecosystem of integrations.

overview: Ray AI Libraries: Data (scalable datasets for ML), Train (distributed training), Tune (hyperparameter tuning), RLlib (reinforcement learning) and Serve (scalable serving).

Ray Core's key abstractions are tasks (stateless functions run in the cluster), actors (stateful worker processes) and objects (immutable values shared across the cluster). The Ray Dashboard and Distributed Debugger help monitor and debug apps.
Install with pip install ray; nightly wheels are on the installation page. Ray is Apache 2.0 licensed.
strengths: Runs on any cloud or Kubernetes
limitations: Best value shows on multi-node workloads
